newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods prices mixed after API delay.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods prices mixed after API delay.

text.p: Spot prices for U.S. West Coast refined products were mixed Tuesday, with afternoon trade drying up after the American Petroleum Institute (API) postponed its Tuesday inventory report, brokers said.

Trade was relatively active early, ahead of the expected report from the API. Players talked Los Angeles CARB-grade unleaded gasoline a quarter cent lower than Monday at 74.25/75.25 cents a gallon, in line with lower NYMEX values.
"Most people were waitng for APIs. A lot of people got done this morning and now it's pretty much dead," a trader said in the afternoon.
Deals were heard done at 75 cents for L.A. CARB gasoline, and 73 cents for San Francisco material, traders said, as players tried squaring positions ahead of U.S. supply data..
A drop in NYMEX crude prices and APIs postponement discouraged buyers late in the day, traders said,
Meanwhile, crude and coker units at Exxon's Benecia refinery near San Francisco were rumored to return to service this week, but the company was not immediately available for comment.
Distillates were little changed, with low sulphur diesel flat at 62/63 cents and bids for CARB diesel up a half-cent at 72.50 cents.
